$comment: FC17.9(a) Cycle 3 (D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-TIMED) — the C11 <threads.h> TIMED-WAIT witness on 4 legs. thrd_sleep, mtx_timedlock and cnd_timedwait were undeclared on EVERY object format until this cycle while `__STDC_NO_THREADS__` was defined on none. elf x86_64 + arm64 (qemu) resolve all three as DIRECT libc.so.6 FFI (glibc 2.39, `nm -D --defined-only` verified on BOTH arches: thrd_sleep@@GLIBC_2.28 WEAK, mtx_timedlock@@GLIBC_2.34 and cnd_timedwait@@GLIBC_2.34 strong). pe64 SYNTHESIZES them over kernel32 — thrd_sleep a capped Sleep loop, mtx_timedlock a TryEnterCriticalSection/GetSystemTimeAsFileTime deadline loop (Win32 has no timed critical-section acquire), cnd_timedwait a single-block SleepConditionVariableCS with the absolute deadline converted to a relative millisecond timeout and the verdict read from GetLastError. macho SYNTHESIZES them over libSystem — thrd_sleep a DIRECT nanosleep, cnd_timedwait a DIRECT pthread_cond_timedwait with the errno mapped, and mtx_timedlock the same deadline loop as pe because pthread_mutex_timedlock is ABSENT FROM DARWIN (measured by link probe). ★★ THIS EXAMPLE EXISTS BECAUSE THE FAILURE MODE IS INVISIBLE TO A COMPILE-ONLY PIN: a timed wait that returns instantly, or one that never returns, compiles perfectly. ★★ SO EACH FUNCTION IS PINNED FROM BOTH SIDES — mtx_timedlock must time out on a mutex another thread holds AND wait-then-succeed on one that thread is about to release; cnd_timedwait must time out unsignalled AND wake when signalled. A constant thrd_timedout passes one arm and fails the other; a constant thrd_success likewise. ★★ AND IT POISONS `struct timespec` TO 0xFF BEFORE ASSIGNING: tv_nsec is `long` — 8 bytes on LP64, FOUR on pe/LLP64 — at offset 8 of a 16-byte struct on both, so no size or offset check can discriminate and a cleanly-zeroed struct hides an 8-byte read of a 4-byte field. With the poison in place that misread folds 0xFFFFFFFF into the high half: the sleep computes a negative millisecond count and returns instantly, and every deadline lands in the distant past so even the ACQUIRE arms report thrd_timedout. ★ NO ARM DEPENDS ON A RACE: every mutex is locked by main BEFORE the thread that probes it exists, and cnd_timedwait releases its mutex atomically so the signaller cannot run ahead of the wait. ⚠⚠ AND NO ARM WAITS OUT A DEADLINE, which is a deliberate design against a MEASURED host defect rather than a shortcut. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-01 with a gcc-built control on this project's WSL leg: CLOCK_REALTIME steps +29 s / -27 s about every five seconds while CLOCK_MONOTONIC stays exact (1100 ms for a 1100 ms nanosleep, 8 of 8). C11 states both deadlines in TIME_UTC, so on such a host a wait for a deadline two seconds out can legitimately last thirty — past the examples runner's own 5 s kRunBudget hang detector, which must NOT be widened to accommodate one example. So the timeout arms use a deadline a MINUTE IN THE PAST (must refuse instantly; a ±30 s step cannot drag it into the future) and the acquire arms one a minute AHEAD, ended by another thread releasing the lock or signalling rather than by the clock. Every verdict is a property of the implementation, none of the clock, and the whole program finishes in about 1.5 s. Only thrd_sleep asserts elapsed time — it can, being RELATIVE and monotone-backed on all three platforms — with a ONE-SIDED bound (>= 1 s, so a forward step still passes) and two retries so a backward step does not red, while a no-op sleep reads 0 on every attempt. Fold-resistant — a real Sleep/nanosleep/kernel wait cannot be const-folded, so the release arm runs the true path.
